races.name: Auto Services Perth Supporting Dundee Bairns Novices' Limited Handicap Steeple Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Dunkerque
runners_data.note: A high-class novice chaser rated OR 132 with five wins from seven starts, including four successive victories on Good ground — his sim-going record of 6W from 15 runs on similar surfaces is outstanding; Quinlan partners a horse in form (won last two), fresh off 18 days' rest under a yard (Candlish T14: 1/13) that has been quiet but firing selectively, and Dunkerque's prominent style means he will eyeball Follow Your Luck throughout in this match-race scenario.
runners_data.comment: Dunkerque arrives in career-best form, winning four of his last five starts with a second the only blemish, and he returns fit just 18 days after his latest victory; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 164 lb is the one thing to watch.

runners_data.name: Follow Your Luck
runners_data.note: A five-year-old front-runner whose entire tactical identity depends on leading and controlling tempo — that is fully available to him here given no other pace rival; Hughes takes the ride for the Patrick Neville yard (T14: 0/7, subdued form), and while Follow Your Luck's sim-going record on Good is just 0W1P from three runs, he has won twice on Soft, suggesting faster conditions represent a slight question mark against a well-credentialled opponent.
runners_data.comment: Follow Your Luck arrives in flying form, a winner three of his last four starts with a third last time out the only blot, and he handles today's distance and going — the chief question is whether 154 lb blunts his finishing kick.

races.paceDynamic: Follow Your Luck is the sole confirmed front-runner in this two-horse contest and will lead from the outset under Brian Hughes, setting a sustainable gallop over 2m4f on Good ground at Perth with zero pressure from behind. Dunkerque, ridden prominently by Sean Quinlan, will track Follow Your Luck closely throughout — in a field of two, this effectively means the pair will race in tandem for the vast majority of the trip, with the real contest beginning at the final fences. This race shape is unusually simple: a controlled, single-file procession that will develop into a two-horse jumping battle from the home turn, with the winner decided by class, jumping accuracy and stamina reserves in the closing stages. The shape marginally favours Dunkerque's prominent-chasing profile given his superior OR, form, and proven ability on Good ground, but Follow Your Luck's front-running comfort means the lead scenario carries genuine weight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Held On
scenarios.trigger: If Follow Your Luck jumps cleanly and dictates an uncontested, measured gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: Follow Your Luck settles into his natural front-running rhythm with no rival to force the pace higher, conserving energy for the finish; Hughes can control the tempo entirely and build a decisive jump advantage if Dunkerque makes an error.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Dunkerque Wears Down Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Dunkerque travels powerfully in behind and reels in Follow Your Luck from the second-last fence.
scenarios.body: Quinlan keeps Dunkerque within striking distance throughout and the superior OR (132 vs 122) tells from two out as the higher-class horse asserts; Dunkerque's six wins from 15 runs on Good ground underline his suitability to these conditions.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Jumping Error Changes Race
scenarios.trigger: If either runner makes a significant blunder at a fence that materially disrupts their momentum or position.
scenarios.body: A loose jumper or costly mistake by either horse in a two-runner race immediately hands the advantage to the other; this scenario is entirely dependent on a specific jumping incident rather than any tactical shift.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Dramatic Last-Fence Finish
scenarios.trigger: If both horses are inseparable entering the last and the race is decided by the final jump and flat sprint.
scenarios.body: With only two runners tracking each other throughout, this outcome is possible but unlikely given the class and fitness edge Dunkerque holds; a clean jump at the last from either horse would likely be sufficient to seal the result before a sprint develops.

watchPoints.text: Follow Your Luck's jumping must be monitored closely — as a front-runner in a two-horse field, any fence error will be immediately punishing with no cover and no room to recover position.
Dunkerque is 18 days fresh; Jennie Candlish's yard is 1/13 over 14 days suggesting the stable is not in peak flow, and backers should watch the market move for confidence signals.
Follow Your Luck's Good-ground record (0W1P from three comparable starts) is noticeably weaker than his Soft-ground form — watch whether the Going sticks at Good or eases before the off.

With only two runners, there is no pace scenario involving pressure or tactical complexity — the entire race hinges on jumping fluency and which horse has most left from two fences out; watch the jumping of both horses at fences 3 and 4 for early indicators.

races.name: Auto Services Volkswagen Commercial Aftersales Novices' Hurdle Race (GBB Race)
Auto Services Perth 24-Hour Recovery Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Castleheath
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse trained by Ciaran Murphy and ridden by Sean Bowen, who brings strong Good-ground form (won on Good, placed twice from five similar-going runs); 36 days since last run is not a concern, and dropping from 16f+ trips to 2m looks a potential advantage if the pace is genuine and he gets a clear run from the second-last.
runners_data.comment: Castleheath shapes as the one to beat on our ratings, and his recent second reads well, while he has run over today's trip and going before; winless in his last four starts, but 168 lb is stiff and connections will need a clear run to get the best from him.

runners_data.name: Scriabin
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who has won and been placed multiple times over this exact trip on Good ground at this venue; Patrick Wadge partners a horse who needs to hold off Nobotheratall early, and if he can dictate terms rather than brawl, his record of nine Good-ground runs with one win and five places makes him a live contender throughout.
runners_data.comment: Scriabin won two starts back and was second three starts back, and he has run over this trip and going before, and his 113 rating marks him as a leading threat; the question is whether he can bounce back from an eighth last time out.

runners_data.name: Nobotheratall
runners_data.note: The other confirmed pace-setter, returned five wins and two places from eight Good-ground starts and arrives in solid form with a 51-day break; Derek Fox will be keen to use his natural speed, but a head-to-head duel with Scriabin over only 2m risks draining both — his recent step up to 2m4f form suggests stamina is fine but he may be vulnerable late.
runners_data.comment: Nobotheratall landed a win three starts back and filled the runner-up spot two starts back, and has run over this trip and going before; the concern is a 51-day absence under 157 lb.

runners_data.name: Try Them
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who won over this course and distance on Good last time out; Brian Hughes will likely slot in just behind the front-runners and the 4yo's recent C&D win is the most obvious form reference in the race, though two successive 5ths prior suggest consistency can waver.
runners_data.comment: Try Them arrives in fair recent nick — a winner last time and second two starts back — but carrying 156 lb, our rating ranks him seventh of eight runners, making him hard to fancy despite the distance and going experience.

runners_data.name: Inappropriate
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse carrying tongue-tie and a strong recent profile — won over Good going, placed three more times from five similar-going starts — with Sean Quinlan retaining the ride; only 13 days since last run could be a minor energy flag, but the shorter 2m trip may suit this horse's late-running style better than the 2m4f+ trips he has contested.
runners_data.comment: Inappropriate shaped with promise when second two starts back, has run over today's trip and going, and at 112 on our rating ranks as a leading threat in this field; the risk is that he has been winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Pure Gold
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up performer whose last five runs show four fourths and a third, consistently failing to win but placing on Good ground; Lisa Harrison's runner is displaced to midfield on the pace map given the volume of hold-up types, meaning its natural style may be compromised and that positional disadvantage tempers its winning prospects here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Pure Gold has placed third two runs back but otherwise struggled to convert consistency into results; she has run over today's trip and going before, and 152 lb is a stiff ask for a mare yet to land a race in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Just Dottie
runners_data.note: Veteran 8yo who carries a tongue-tie and hold-up profile, but with Miss Becky Smith claiming 7lbs the partnership has a useful weight advantage; her best form figures over this trip on Good ground are promising, but she too is a true rear-runner squeezed into a midfield slot by the shape of this race, making her role harder than her natural instincts prefer.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in her last five starts, Just Dottie nonetheless showed a third two runs back to suggest she retains ability, and she has run over today's trip and going before; a burden of 149 lb is the concern.

runners_data.name: Elemental Eye
runners_data.note: Arrived on an 8-day turnaround for Iain Jardine who has a modest 14-day record (4/27); the 5yo has won and placed over Good going and shorter trips, and is a hold-up horse that the pace map places in midfield — among the three redistributed types, his recent 2m2f experience is closest to this trip and he retains modest upside if traffic allows a clean late run.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts, with finishes of seventh, ninth and eighth, Elemental Eye has little recent form to recommend him, and our figures rank him last of the eight runners here; his experience over today's trip and a quick turnaround eight days ago are modest consolations at best.

races.paceDynamic: Scriabin and Nobotheratall are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the off over this 2m trip at Perth, creating a genuinely contested pace rather than a dawdle — on Good ground this should produce an honest, rhythmic gallop across the eight hurdles. Try Them will push forward to dispute or sit just off the pace, compressing the field early and ensuring no one gets an easy lead without a fight. This race shape — two legitimate front-runners duelling with a prominent type pressing — classically suits horses who can travel fluidly in behind and pick up with one run from the second-last, making midfield-to-hold-up horses the primary beneficiaries, provided they are genuine in that role. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Pure Gold, Just Dottie, and Elemental Eye are true hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map; of these, Elemental Eye's recent course-and-distance form gives it the best chance of actually being positioned where it needs to be, though all three may find themselves racing less than ideally placed given the pace scenario.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Scriabin and Nobotheratall burn each other up through a genuine early gallop and the field races at an honest clip throughout.
scenarios.body: The duel between the two front-runners uses their reserves across 2m on Good ground, leaving the door open for a horse who has travelled sweetly in midfield to sweep past from the second-last flight; Castleheath and Inappropriate are both course-profiled hold-up horses with Good-ground form who can deliver a single telling run.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dominates Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two front-runners — most likely Scriabin given stronger lead history at this trip — gains a clear early advantage and is allowed to dictate a controlled, measured pace.
scenarios.body: With a sustainable gallop rather than a true duel, the leader conserves energy and the hold-up horses never generate enough momentum to peg them back over just 2m; Scriabin's record of two wins and five places from nine Good-ground starts underlines this suitability.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Outstay Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuine but the hold-up horses fail to close — being out of position — and a prominent racer saves ground from just off the lead.
scenarios.body: Try Them, who won over this C&D on Good going last time, sits a length or two off the duel and pounces at the second-last as the front-runners weaken; Nobotheratall, dropping from 2m4f where he won and ran well, may also find this trip sharp enough to sustain a late surge from just off the pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly fierce and the entire front rank ties up simultaneously, creating a vacuum for true closers to come from well off the bridle.
scenarios.body: Pure Gold, Just Dottie, and Elemental Eye are all genuine hold-up types but each is likely displaced in the field map; with STYLE_FIT tags signalling they may not find their natural rear position, this scenario is structurally unlikely — Elemental Eye's two-mile wins give it the best claim if it does get a true rails run late.

watchPoints.text: Scriabin and Nobotheratall will lock horns for the lead from flag to flag — if neither concedes, watch for both to empty approaching the final hurdle, leaving the race wide open for anything tracking them.

Try Them won over this C&D last time and Brian Hughes will be intent on getting a prominent pitch — if he pushes to the front group early, a three-way pace battle develops and the race could become truly strong.

Inappropriate is only 13 days off his last run; watch his behaviour in the paddock and early jumping for any signs that the quick turnaround has left him short, as his hold-up profile requires him to travel well throughout.

Pure Gold, Just Dottie, and Elemental Eye are all genuine hold-up types likely to find themselves further forward than ideal — watch where they actually settle in the first half-mile, as any who successfully drop to the rear may be better placed than the pace map implies.

Castleheath has strong Good-ground form but ran in a 168f race last time — monitor how he handles the drop to a sharper 2m at Perth where getting a clear passage from the back is not guaranteed in an 8-runner field.

races.name: Auto Services Mercedes Benz Truck Aftersales Handicap Steeple Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Regal Renaissance
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner in the field who has won three of her last four on similar Good ground; Sean Bowen takes the ride for a trainer in decent 14-day form (2/16), and a 47-day break is worth monitoring at an age-8 mark, though her prominent style is perfectly aligned with this race shape.
runners_data.comment: Regal Renaissance arrives here in fine heart, winning three of her last five starts with a victory two runs back, and she handles today's distance and going, making her the clear profile pick despite a 47-day absence and 168 lb to carry.

runners_data.name: Wasdell Dundalk
runners_data.note: An 11-year-old hold-up horse whose form reads 642P recently though he has finished placed on Good ground across similar trips; Callum Bewley takes over from the saddle for a trainer with just 0/2 in the 14-day window, and 57 days off adds a small fitness question to a horse already needing things to fall right from the rear.
runners_data.comment: Rated highest in the field and has run over this trip before, Wasdell Dundalk catches the eye on the back of a runner-up finish one start ago and has experience of today's distance and going; the main concern is the pullup last time out after 57 days off, leaving his current fitness an open question.

runners_data.name: No Regrets
runners_data.note: Nicky Richards' 12-year-old arrives on the back of two recent placed efforts including a win, and Danny McMenamin is a solid booking; his hold-up style suits a scenario where the front-runner is run down over the final stages, though a 93-day break is the most notable concern here and his best form has come on Soft rather than Good.
runners_data.comment: No Regrets shaped as a genuine threat when a close second last time out, and was a winner two starts back; he has experience of today's trip and conditions, and a rating of 114 underlines his claims — the main concern is whether 93 days off the track leaves him short of peak fitness.

runners_data.name: Inis Oirr
runners_data.note: Strong recent form with three consecutive placed efforts including a win, and the Lucinda Russell & Michael Scudamore yard is well-respected for staying chasers; in truth this is a horse that races from the rear, and the 10lb claimer Gregor Walkingshaw taking off that weight is an interesting angle, though racing outside his natural position will blunt his effectiveness in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Inis Oirr arrives here with a fine run of form — second two starts back and third last time out — and he has experience of today's distance and going, so conditions should hold no fears; the main concern is a 57-day absence.

runners_data.name: Sir Carnegie
runners_data.note: The youngest and lowest-rated in the field at OR 101, Brian Hughes is a high-quality pilot and Mickey Bowen's stable is firing well at 6/23 in 14-day form; genuinely a hold-up type who has shown he can win (twice from last five), the hood goes on for the first time which is worth noting, and only 16 days since last run suggests freshness is not a concern — but he is being shown in midfield away from his favoured rear-rank position.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins three and four starts back give Sir Carnegie some profile, but he has finished fifth and sixth in his last two outings and is ranked last of the five runners on our figures, making him difficult to recommend despite a trainer hitting 26% in the last 14 days.

races.paceDynamic: Regal Renaissance is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-runner field and, with no genuine pace rival to challenge her, she is set to dictate from the front at a controlled, sustainable gallop over the 3m trip on Good ground at Perth. The four remaining runners — Wasdell Dundalk, No Regrets, Inis Oirr, and Sir Carnegie — are all hold-up types by nature, meaning the pace Regal Renaissance sets will be uncontested and she can conserve energy through the early and middle stages before quickening from the front off a relatively honest tempo. This race shape overwhelmingly favours the patient hold-up horses who can track the leader from a distance and pounce off a strong staying finish in the closing stages, with Inis Oirr and Sir Carnegie the redistributed runners who in truth prefer to come from further back but have been mapped forward due to the surplus of rear-rank types this field generates. The tactical verdict is clear: uncontested front-running from Regal Renaissance creates a thorough-staying test, and the horse best able to sustain a long, relentless gallop from off the pace — rather than a sprint finish — will be best placed to capitalise.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Regal Renaissance Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Regal Renaissance bowls along at a measured, uncontested pace and her rivals fail to close the gap in time.
scenarios.body: She dictates every yard of the 3m trip, conserving energy through the middle section before extending at the business end off a comfortable lead; her recent win record at this trip on Good ground (three wins from four similar-going runs) underlines this is the most likely shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Grind Down Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the hold-up horses — particularly No Regrets or Wasdell Dundalk — reel in Regal Renaissance over the final two fences as the pace tells on her off a longer layoff.
scenarios.body: The genuine staying ability of the hold-up brigade becomes decisive as the 47-day absence from Regal Renaissance softens her edge late on; a strong gallop extracts maximum stamina from the field and the closers flourish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Types Capitalise
scenarios.trigger: If Inis Oirr or Sir Carnegie, both true hold-up horses shown in midfield due to redistribution, manage to find a race-saving position and unleash a sustained late run.
scenarios.body: Despite being mapped forward, their natural inclination to race from the rear means they could find momentum if the race develops into a true stamina test over the closing mile; Sir Carnegie's yard is in excellent 14-day form (6/23) which marginally keeps this live.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Disrupted Jumping Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If errors at fences destabilise the race shape — unseats, falls or jumping mistakes — creating a chaotic finish where the race order is reset.
scenarios.body: In a small field of five over fences, any significant jumping incident could hand the race to a rival who avoids trouble; at 3m on Perth's right-handed track, stamina and jumping soundness become the arbiter.

watchPoints.text: Regal Renaissance's 47-day absence is the key risk — if she fails to see out the 3m trip on returning from a break, the hold-up horses will sweep past her from the final fence.
Sir Carnegie's headgear change (hood) is significant to watch in the early stages — if it sharpens him into a more prominent position than expected, the race shape could shift meaningfully.
No Regrets has had a 93-day break and his best form is on Soft ground — if the Good surface blunts his finishing kick, the hold-up scenario collapses and Regal Renaissance benefits further.

Gregor Walkingshaw's 10lb claim on Inis Oirr makes the weight attractive, but in a race where his mount needs to race against its natural style, watch whether the pair can find a rhythm settling further back than the pace map shows.

With all four rivals being hold-up types, watch the early pace — if any of them break sharply and push up to challenge Regal Renaissance, the uncontested lead scenario is immediately undermined and a stronger pace test emerges.

races.name: www.asp.scot Stellantis Commercial Aftersales Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Lets Mingle
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner at OR 111, ridden by claimer Gregor Walkingshaw (10lb); racing prominently is its natural game but the STYLE_FIT flag notes it may be slightly out of its most comfortable role — uncontested pace-setting here should suit regardless, and Perth Good form reads positively from two prior runs.
runners_data.comment: Won two starts back and has run over today's trip and going, Lets Mingle arrives here 23 days fresh, carrying 169 lb, and her rating of 113 marks her as the one to beat in this field of ten, though her fifth last time out is the one minor caution.

runners_data.name: Follow Charlie
runners_data.note: Top recent form (two wins in last five) with the trainer firing at 2/9 over 14 days; a genuine hold-up horse who needs a true pace to reel in the leaders, and Good ground suits based on a win at this track over 2m — trip slightly shorter than ideal but not disqualifying.
runners_data.comment: Follow Charlie won his last two starts and arrives in decent nick 23 days on, with experience of today's trip and going in his favour; the 168 lb burden is a stiff ask, however, and his ranking sixth of ten on our rating suggests he faces better company than his recent wins came against.

runners_data.name: Spit Spot
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for the Russell/Scudamore yard (0/3 T14 — stable not in red-hot form); the tongue-strap is notable, and a 57-day absence requires monitoring — only one win from fifteen runs on Good, making the ground angle mildly concerning despite an OR of 109.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and coming off a fall, Spit Spot nonetheless shapes as a leading threat here — she has experience over today's trip and going, our rating of 111 ranks her second in the field, and 57 days off may have freshened her up, though her recent jumping frailties are the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Lowlands
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer for Nicky Richards (1/2 T14, stable in decent touch); won at 2m on Good and placed twice at 2m-plus, so the trip and surface suit well — Danny McMenamin is a reliable handler in this type of race and 23 days since last run is a fresh but not flat preparation.

runners_data.name: Bogha Baiste
runners_data.note: A five-year-old lightly raced for a young trainer (Lizzie Quinlan, 1/7 T14); all five career runs show place-form rather than wins and the Good ground is untested in this particular race context — 67 days since last run and no headgear worn, suggesting improvement on fitness is possible.
runners_data.comment: Bogha Baiste has shown consistency without a win in recent starts, posting back-to-back thirds before two fourths, though a pulled-up effort on the other side of that sequence gives pause; experience on today's going helps, but 67 days off and 164 lb are notable questions.

runners_data.name: Annie Agnew
runners_data.note: Prominent style in training from Gerald Quinn (0/1 T14); one win from ten on Good ground but a solid four-time placer on similar surfaces — the 5lb claimer Mr D McGill reduces the burden and a handy racing position should keep Annie Agnew involved into the straight.
runners_data.comment: Placed last time out and carrying 161 lb into this, Annie Agnew has run over today's trip and going and rates 6 lb above her official mark — a compelling case for a big run — though she remains winless in her last five starts, which is the key concern.

runners_data.name: Garrick Painter
runners_data.note: Won at 1m6f on Good ground for Noel Kelly (0/14 T14 — stable form is a significant concern) and returned just 12 days ago; in truth a natural hold-up type pushed into the midfield map position because the rear is crowded, and the STYLE_FIT flag means its chance is modestly discounted in a race dominated by front-rank runners.
runners_data.comment: Garrick Painter slipped up last time out and was sixth two starts back, making him hard to fancy ranked eighth of ten on our figures, though he does bring going experience and a win four starts back to the table.

runners_data.name: Kinbara Firstdraft
runners_data.note: Nine-day turnaround is notably quick and the consistent mid-pack finishes (no win since entering the handicap) tell a story of a horse that finds the same level; a genuine hold-up performer by inclination, placed in the midfield map due to congestion at the rear, and the STYLE_FIT flag limits the realistic upside unless the pace genuinely collapses.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Kinbara Firstdraft has at least shown some consistency hitting fourth twice in that sequence, and he has experience over today's trip and going; however, 158 lb is a stiff ask for a horse yet to land a race.

runners_data.name: Hawkseye View
runners_data.note: Absent 149 days (no recent trackwork signals available) and the soft-ground wins raise a mild query about whether this Good Perth surface truly plays to strengths — Peter Kavanagh takes the ride for an OR-90 runner at a career-high relative mark, and any ring rust from the layoff would be a real disadvantage over the sharp Perth circuit.
runners_data.comment: A lengthy absence of 149 days and a run of one win in his last five starts, including a fall, make Hawkseye View hard to fancy here, ranked ninth of ten on our figures, though he has experience of today's distance and going and did score four starts back.

runners_data.name: Tigress Lilly
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up type for the busy Russell/Scudamore yard (0/3 T14); all five recent runs on Good ground show finishes of 5th or worse, and the STYLE_FIT flag reflects that being repositioned into midfield does not replicate the waiting role the horse actually wants — Patrick Wadge faces a stiff task to manufacture momentum from whatever position the race affords.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked bottom of this field on our figures, Tigress Lilly faces a stiff task here; she has run over today's going before and returns after 57 days off, but consistency has been elusive and 146 lb is no help.

races.paceDynamic: Lets Mingle is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no natural rival to push the tempo, is expected to bowl along at a sustainable gallop from flag to finish over this 2m4f Perth trip on Good ground. Spit Spot, Annie Agnew, and Hawkseye View will press forward into prominent positions just off the leader, creating a compact early order but without the headlong speed that would seriously test Lets Mingle's stamina. The hold-up brigade — Follow Charlie, Lowlands, and Bogha Baiste — will need to close ground from further back, but with a controlled pace it is far from certain the race will be truly run to suit deep closers. This shape — an uncontested leader, measured tempo, and a tight early group — strongly favours horses who can race prominently or just off the pace and quicken from a handy position; true hold-up horses face the additional task of making up ground against a race that may never fully string out. The field holds more genuine hold-up types than can all be accommodated at the rear, with Garrick Painter, Kinbara Firstdraft, and Tigress Lilly redistributed to midfield on the map — of the three, Garrick Painter and Kinbara Firstdraft are most likely to actually find cover in the middle pack.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lets Mingle Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Lets Mingle is allowed to bowl along unchallenged and sets a gallop the field cannot disrupt.
scenarios.body: Lets Mingle dictates a measured pace throughout, stealing margins that a compressed field of prominent and hold-up types struggle to claw back on this flat Perth circuit. Horses racing handy — Spit Spot, Annie Agnew — are best placed to respond when the leader kicks, while back-markers face a straightforward winning distance.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Land Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the pace-pressing horses — Spit Spot and Annie Agnew — press Lets Mingle harder than expected and the leader fades in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: A slightly faster-than-anticipated tempo drains Lets Mingle's reserves up the home straight, leaving the prominent challengers — Spit Spot, Annie Agnew — to inherit the lead and fight it out. Horses who travel just off the pace with a turn of foot stand to benefit most in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely honest enough to string the field out and the leaders empty, allowing Follow Charlie or Lowlands to come through late.
scenarios.body: Follow Charlie's recent winning form and Lowlands' strong Good-ground record give these hold-up types a genuine chance if the race develops into a genuine test; both horses have won over similar trips on comparable going. However, the redistribution of several notional hold-up types to midfield positions reduces the likelihood of the race unfolding in a manner that truly rewards deep closers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Produces Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If fallers, jumping errors, or a badly-run race creates gaps that allow a lower-ranked or unexposed runner to emerge.
scenarios.body: Hawkseye View (returned from a 149-day break but has a win on Good ground) or Bogha Baiste (consistent place-form, improved fitness possible) could sneak into contention if the race shape collapses. Kinbara Firstdraft, despite modest recent form, is a true hold-up type out of its natural position and is unlikely to benefit from a chaotic shape.

watchPoints.text: Lets Mingle is uncontested up front — watch whether Gregor Walkingshaw (10lb claimer) sets a genuinely sustainable or dangerously slow tempo, as either extreme could dramatically reshape who benefits.

Follow Charlie and Lowlands are genuine hold-up horses whose chances hinge entirely on the pace being honest enough to close — if Lets Mingle crawls, both are likely to find themselves with too much ground to make up in the short Perth straight.

Garrick Painter, Kinbara Firstdraft, and Tigress Lilly are all true hold-up types crowded out of their natural position; watch for any of them getting boxed in or lacking room on the final bend as they try to manoeuvre from a midfield slot that is not their instinctive starting point.
Spit Spot and Hawkseye View both carry absence flags (57 and 149 days respectively) — watch the pre-race market for any meaningful support that might signal stable confidence after their breaks.
Trainer Noel Kelly's 14-day strike rate of 0/14 for Garrick Painter is a sharp negative — watch whether the market reflects inside knowledge to the contrary or simply confirms the stat.

races.name: Auto Services Perth Sales And Rentals Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Down Around
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's 9-year-old has excellent Good-going credentials (2 wins and 5 places from 15 similar-surface runs) and races prominently, placing him perfectly to track Burgundy Man and strike in the closing stages; 7 days since his last run suggests he is fit and freshened, and the tongue-strap headgear is retained.
runners_data.comment: Bounced back to win two starts back before a fourth last time out, and Down Around has experience of today's distance and going to call on; back within a week and carrying 168 lb, he arrives fit and ready to go.

runners_data.name: Midnight Moonshine
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type who has struggled for form lately (best effort a 5th), ridden by a 7lb claimer in Miss Becky Smith for trainer R Mike Smith, and returning from 34 days off; the combination of amateur jockey, modest recent figures, and a busy hold-up market makes this a tough assignment.
runners_data.comment: Ranked top of the eight on our rating, Midnight Moonshine has run over today's trip and going before and returns after a 34-day break potentially freshened up, though his heavy burden of 168 lb is the chief concern given he is yet to score in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Sauce Of Life
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who brings a recent win over 20f at Southwell on Soft going, and while his similar-going record is moderate (1W1P from 10), Nicky Richards keeps him fresh with only 2 runners in 14 days; the hood is retained and at 3m he has the stamina to sit handy and challenge, though 86 days off is a slight concern.
runners_data.comment: Sauce Of Life landed a win four starts back and has experience of today's trip and conditions, with our rating of 104 putting him narrowly ahead of most rivals; the main concern is a return from 86 days off following a pulled up effort two starts back.

runners_data.name: Dalileo
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins on Good ground over 24f give him strong credentials, and while he is a hold-up horse who drops back on the map, his class (OR 100) and proven finishing ability make him the most dangerous closer in the field if he gets a clean run; trainer Lisa Harrison sends him with low recent activity (0/2 in 14 days).
runners_data.comment: Dalileo won back-to-back in his last five starts but has since disappointed with a seventh, and 163 lb is a stiff ask; he has run over today's trip and going, though our rating of 96 leaves him with something to find on the figures.

runners_data.name: Theirshegoes
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up operator by style — her two Good-going runs in this distance bracket show she can get involved late, but she carries a style-fit discount (0.92) as the hold-up market is crowded; 54 days since her last run and a 7lb-claiming jockey in Joshua Thompson add further caution.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked sixth of eight here, Theirshegoes does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and her second last time out shows she retains ability; 54 days off and a hefty 153 lb are the obstacles to overcome.

runners_data.name: Le Grand Vert
runners_data.note: Won over 25f on Good going and placed over 26f on Good, so the stamina is proven, and Sean Quinlan is an experienced pilot — but he is a true hold-up horse squeezed into the midfield map position; the tongue-plate and 10-day turnaround suggest he is cherry-ripe, though his recent form (P68) is modest, and being out of his natural rear-of-field role tempers expectations.
runners_data.comment: Fresh from a run 10 days ago, Le Grand Vert brings distance and going experience to the table, and a rating of 100 gives him strong claims here; the concern is his recent sequence of an eighth and sixth in his last two starts.

runners_data.name: C'Mon So
runners_data.note: A 5-year-old hold-up type by trade, but his entire recent form reads 6s and 9s on Good ground and he has never won in seven similar-going runs; Derek Fox is a capable jockey for Lucinda Russell and Michael Scudamore, but 67 days off and a style-fit discount (0.91) leave this runner with the least compelling profile in the race.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked seventh of eight on our figures, C'Mon So faces a stiff ask here; he hasn't troubled the judge in recent outings, though experience over today's trip and going, plus 67 days of freshening up, offer modest crumbs of comfort.

runners_data.name: Burgundy Man
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner who will control the pace from flag to finish — his recent form (6-P9PP) and total absence of wins from five Good-going starts are serious flags, suggesting he is a reliable pace-setter but an unlikely winner; Toby Wynne for R Mike Smith must keep it sensible, as this horse is likely to be passed in the closing stages.
runners_data.comment: Burgundy Man has pulled up three times in his last five starts and is winless in that spell, making him very difficult to fancy ranked last on our figures; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 23 days between runs at least suggests he arrives fresh.

races.paceDynamic: Burgundy Man is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no serious challenger for the lead in a 3m Perth hurdle on Good ground, he will bowl along at a comfortable, self-regulated tempo from the outset. Down Around and Sauce Of Life will press forward into prominent positions directly behind him, creating a small, settled lead group rather than a contested gallop. This field contains more hold-up horses than the race shape can naturally accommodate — Theirshegoes, Le Grand Vert, and C'Mon So are genuine hold-up types but are mapped to midfield because the rear is overcrowded with closers; they are unlikely to get the wide, clean passage late that their style ideally requires, with Le Grand Vert and Theirshegoes the most experienced at this trip and the likeliest to find cover efficiently. A sustainable, front-runner-controlled pace over 3m on Good ground at Perth strongly favours horses racing prominently who can track the pace and strike from 2-3 out, before the back-markers can wind up their challenge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Burgundy Man Controls, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Burgundy Man sets a steady, uncontested pace and the race develops as a controlled test of stamina from the front.
scenarios.body: Burgundy Man dictates from the front on Good ground over 3m, with Down Around and Sauce Of Life sitting close enough to strike turning in; the steady pace means those racing prominently conserve energy and have first run on the closers. Down Around's record on Good going (2 wins, 5 places from 15 similar-going runs) and Gordon Elliott's in-form yard (2/35 in 14 days) make him the natural beneficiary of this shape, while Sauce Of Life's prominent style and recent win give him claims.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Dalileo Makes Late Ground
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely steady enough to compress the finish and Dalileo, a proven winner over 24f on Good ground twice in succession, gets a clear run from the rear.
scenarios.body: Dalileo's hold-up style and proven finishing kick (back-to-back wins on Good ground) mean a genuinely slow early pace can suit him if the race develops into a sprint finish; he will need a clear passage but has the class rating to warrant respect. Peter Kavanagh must position him well early to avoid being caught flat-footed in a compressed finish, but his two recent wins at 24f suggest the extra 2f here is not certain to help.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Attrition Test, Stamina Paramount
scenarios.trigger: If Burgundy Man gradually increases tempo from halfway, turning the race into a sustained stamina test that strings the field out.
scenarios.body: A stronger gallop set by Burgundy Man would ruthlessly expose any hold-up horses lacking the stamina for 3m on Good Perth ground, reducing the field to those with proven staying credentials; Down Around's 3m history and Dalileo's bold jumping record become critical. Midnight Moonshine, a genuine hold-up type with amateur jockey Miss Becky Smith, is likely to find this shape most damaging given his modest recent form and 34-day absence.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Swamp Tiring Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Burgundy Man's lack of a recent win (0 wins from 5 similar-going runs) sees him fade dramatically from 2 out, leaving the door open to hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: In this unlikely shape, Burgundy Man's poor record (6-P9PP recent form) catches up with him and he capitulates suddenly in the closing stages, briefly creating a gap for hold-up horses; however, Theirshegoes, Le Grand Vert, and C'Mon So are all racing somewhat out of their natural role and carry reduced style-fit scores, making this scenario the least likely to fully materialise. Le Grand Vert has the strongest hold-up credentials of the trio and the most course-relevant win in his history.

watchPoints.text: Burgundy Man's stamina — watch whether he begins to shorten stride and capitulate between the second-last and last hurdle, as this is the moment Down Around and Sauce Of Life will make their winning moves.

Le Grand Vert and Theirshegoes are genuine hold-up horses forced into midfield by a crowded rear; watch how Sean Quinlan and Joshua Thompson manage traffic from the halfway point, as a poor position could end their challenge before the home turn.

Sauce Of Life is returning from 86 days off for Nicky Richards — watch his jumping fluency early, as a jumping error from a prominent position over 3m on Good ground could cost him any winning chance.

Down Around has Gordon Elliott's backing (2/35 in 14 days) and is fresh off a 7-day turnaround — watch whether Sean Bowen sends him into second immediately after the first hurdle to ensure he is on the heels of Burgundy Man throughout.

Dalileo has won twice in a row on Good going and is the form horse in the field at OR 100 — watch whether Peter Kavanagh can get him to travel comfortably in the first half of the race, as a strong finish depends entirely on a trouble-free passage off the final bend.
